title: Building a Retailer Pitch Deck: What Buyers Actually Want to See
summary: What retail buyers actually look for in a pitch deck: the slides, data, and proof points that move a supplier from first meeting to purchase order.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


The five core metrics merchants evaluate in the first five minutes of a pitch


-


How to organize slides using category gap data, sales velocity, and margin math


-


Why detailing lead times, logistics, and fulfillment capacity secures buyer confidence


Retail buyers evaluate pitch decks through a commercial lens rather than an investor mindset. Within the first few minutes of a meeting, merchants work through a checklist covering category fit, projected sales velocity, margin structure, promotional investment, and supply chain reliability. Securing shelf space requires structuring your presentation around category data and operational execution, reserving brand backstory for a brief supporting role later in the deck.


## What Is the Retail Buyer Mental Checklist?


First-time suppliers frequently construct pitch presentations modeled on investor pitches, leading with founder origin stories, personal mission statements, and product passion. While venture capitalists invest in long-term founder trajectories, retail category managers oversee finite planograms, strict financial targets, and inventory turn requirements.


When walking into a line review or new item pitch, merchants evaluate five core criteria:


-


**Category fit:** Does this product address an unfulfilled shopper need or replace an underperforming item, avoiding redundant duplication of existing shelf inventory?


-


**Expected velocity:** How many units and dollar sales will this item generate per store per week?


-


**Store margin:** What net profitability does the retailer retain after factoring in wholesale pricing, landed costs, and promotional allowances?


-


**Promotional support:** What marketing campaigns, ad features, and trade spend will the brand commit to drive shopper trial and sell-through?


-


**Supply reliability:** Can the supplier consistently deliver order quantities on time and in full without causing out-of-stock events?


Structuring your pitch deck around these five decisions aligns your presentation directly with merchant priorities.


## How Should You Structure a Data-Driven Pitch Deck for Retailers?


To make a compelling commercial case, sequence your presentation slides to answer merchant questions in order.


### 1. Lead with the Category Opportunity


Opening slides must establish an objective argument for the buyer's category using empirical market data. Identify specific category gaps, such as underperforming subcategories, missing price tiers, or changing consumer habits that current shelf offerings fail to address.


Suppliers can substantiate category gaps using point-of-sale (POS) data from existing accounts or third-party syndicated research from organizations like SPINS or Nielsen. Analyzing planogram pricing and product positioning demonstrates thorough market preparation. Only after defining the category opportunity should you present your product as the commercial solution.


**Related Reading:**[Modular Resets Explained: What New Suppliers Need to Know About the Mod Cycle](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/modular-resets-explained-what-new-suppliers-need-to-know-about-the-mod-cycle)


### 2. Present Sales Velocity and Practical Proxies


Sales velocity, measured in units sold per store per week, serves as the clearest indicator of whether a product earns its physical footprint on a shelf. When sales history exists, display velocity figures plainly alongside store counts, retailer names, and reporting timeframes.


Suppliers lacking established retail distribution should present honest proxy metrics labeled clearly:


-


Direct-to-consumer (DTC) sell-through and repeat purchase metrics


-


Sales velocity from regional, independent, or specialty retail accounts


-


Syndicated category benchmarks for comparable items at similar price points


Existing distribution at competing retailers can also strengthen your position. Demonstrating strong annual sales across regional competitors highlights existing consumer demand that the target merchant currently misses.


**Related Reading:**[How to Prepare for Your First Modular: A Timeline for New Suppliers](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-prepare-for-your-first-modular-a-timeline-for-new-suppliers)


### 3. Lay Out Complete Pricing and Margin Math


Merchants require complete pricing transparency and should never have to calculate profitability during a pitch. Dedicate a slide to breaking down financial terms explicitly, drawing on proven[retail financial formulas](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/win-at-retail-with-the-right-metrics) :


-


**Landed cost (store cost):** Total cost to deliver one unit to the retailer, including freight, duties, and handling


-


**Wholesale price:** The price charged directly to the retailer per unit


-


**Suggested retail price (SRP):** The recommended shelf price for consumers


-


**Resulting margin:** Retailer profit expressed as both a percentage and in dollar terms per unit


Dollar margin per unit, known as penny profit, represents the absolute dollar return generated per unit sold. Lower-priced items with high percentage margins can generate minimal dollar profit, whereas higher-priced items with moderate percentage margins yield significant penny profit. Demonstrating both metrics ensures merchants evaluate total category profitability.


Before entering negotiations, determine your floor cost down to the penny. Leave sufficient margin to absorb future[promotional allowances, markdowns, and trade spend](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/the-true-cost-of-selling-to-retailers-slotting-trade-spend-and-deductions) .


### 4. Close with Operations and Logistics Confidence


Operational logistics represent a critical section that early-stage suppliers frequently omit. Establishing logistical readiness transforms buyer interest into a confirmed relationship. Detail your execution capabilities clearly:


-


Production lead times and current manufacturing capacity


-


GTIN rules and[master carton specifications and case pack configurations](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/case-pack-configuration-how-to-build-a-pack-that-works-at-retail)


-


Fulfillment methods, whether shipping via direct-store-delivery, 3PL partners, or wholesale distributors


-


Existing compliance with retailer routing guides or electronic data interchange (EDI) standards


Request distribution footprints conservatively. Pitching immediate national distribution across massive retail footprints can overwhelm production capacity, leading to compliance fines and scorecard penalties. Recommending regional distribution centers or targeted store clusters proves operational maturity.


**Related Reading:**[What Happens After a Retailer Says Yes: The First 90 Days for a New Supplier](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-happens-after-a-retailer-says-yes-the-first-90-days-for-a-new-supplier)


## Where Does Brand Story Belong in the Presentation?


Brand origin, founder mission, and team background play a genuine supporting role in retail pitches. After establishing financial and category metrics, a brief brand story provides distinct identity, highlights unique product attributes, and builds personal rapport.


Position the brand story around slide seven or eight, keeping the narrative under ninety seconds. Highlight key differentiators such as proprietary formulations, clean ingredient certifications, or relevant team expertise. At this stage, brand history serves as validation for an already sound commercial proposal.


## Lessons from Walmart's Open Call Program


Real-world retailer submission programs demonstrate that buyer expectations are concrete and standardized.[Walmart's Open Call program](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-prepare-for-walmarts-open-call) , hosted annually since 2013, invites entrepreneurs to pitch products grown, made, or assembled in the United States.


Applicants submit product details through RangeMe for evaluation by merchant teams. Selected suppliers secure 30-minute one-on-one meetings with category buyers in Bentonville.


A 30-minute meeting window demands strict efficiency. Spending ten minutes on founder background leaves insufficient time to address category growth, margin math, and supply chain readiness. Successful Open Call participants present clear pricing, propose realistic regional store counts, and demonstrate transparent volume capacity.


While pitch deck agencies and competition testimonials showcase wins, treat brief promotional claims as encouragement. Ground your pitch strategy in documented retailer guidelines and verified metrics.


**Related Reading:**[Your First Vendor Scorecard: Reading Fill Rate, OTIF, and Chargeback Metrics](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/your-first-vendor-scorecard-reading-fill-rate-otif-and-chargeback-metrics)


## Essential Materials to Bring to the Buyer Meeting


In addition to your primary presentation, prepare supporting materials to leave with the category buyer:


-


**One-page sell sheet:** A single-page document summarizing UPCs, case pack dimensions, wholesale cost, SRP, margin structure, and contact information.


-


**Concise slide deck:** Keep the primary deck under ten slides to maintain focus during short meetings.


-


**Product samples:** Confirm buyer preferences through your broker before bringing physical samples, as some buyers focus strictly on commercial numbers.


Working alongside an experienced retail broker helps pre-position your product, navigate account-specific requirements, and manage meeting dynamics effectively.


## Streamlining Retail Data for Pitch Success


Building a persuasive buyer pitch requires consolidating data across disparate sales channels, regional accounts, and syndicated reports. Emerging suppliers often spend preparation time manually compiling inconsistent portal exports into spreadsheets.


Having access to clear, centralized performance data ensures your numbers withstand buyer scrutiny. Understanding point-of-sale (POS) data and sales velocity provides the baseline for these conversations. Solutions like[SPS Analytics](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/analytics/) integrate point-of-sale data, inventory metrics, and item performance into unified reporting, empowering suppliers to present accurate numbers with confidence during line reviews.
